jobs.title: Catastrophe Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Business Analyst (BA) works as a member of the Catastrophe (CAT) Planning & Logistics Team, supporting efforts to ensure organizational readiness and effective response to catastrophe events. The BA leverages data, mapping technology, analysis, and collaboration to support catastrophe planning, logistics, claims readiness, and response activities.

Working with CAT Planning & Logistics, Claims, and other internal and external partners, the BA collects, analyzes, and communicates information to support business decisions, improve processes, strengthen readiness, and help coordinate resources and services following disasters.

Job Duties

Establishes collaborative relationships with CAT Planning & Logistics, Claims, and other business partners.
Collects, analyzes, and communicates data to support catastrophe planning, readiness, logistics, and response.
Uses data, mapping systems, and other tools to assess catastrophe events and communicate potential and actual impacts.
Supports the development and continuous improvement of CAT plans, processes, procedures, reporting, and readiness activities.
Supports the development, implementation, and maintenance of catastrophe response and logistics plans, helping ensure both short- and long-term organizational readiness.
Collects, analyzes, organizes, and communicates catastrophe-related data to support planning, response, and business decision-making.
Uses mapping and Geographic Information Systems (GIS), data visualization, and other analytical tools to evaluate catastrophe events, geographic impacts, exposures, and other information relevant to CAT response.
Supports the coordination, communication, tracking, and reporting of Catastrophe Claims events, providing timely and accurate information to business partners and leadership.
Assists with the development of catastrophe event updates, reports, maps, dashboards, presentations, and other materials used to communicate event-specific information and support decision-making.
Supports the planning and coordination of CAT readiness exercises and drills to evaluate Claims readiness, identify potential limitations, and strengthen response capabilities.
Assists with the development and maintenance of CAT plans, playbooks, procedures, process flows, and other readiness documentation.
Supports the coordination of resources, equipment, supplies, personnel, and logistics necessary for catastrophe response, working with internal and external partners as appropriate.
Analyzes current processes and identifies opportunities to improve CAT planning, logistics, reporting, data utilization, and response capabilities.
Organizes and conducts meetings, briefings, exercises, and demonstrations. Prepares supporting materials, documents outcomes, and tracks action items and commitments.
Works collaboratively with business and technical teams to identify requirements and support the development or enhancement of tools and solutions used for CAT planning, analysis, logistics, and response.
Supports continuous improvement following catastrophe events and readiness exercises by assisting with after-action reviews, documenting lessons learned, identifying gaps, and tracking improvement activities.
Performs assigned CAT planning, analysis, logistics, and project activities to committed effort and dates and provides support during catastrophe events as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree preferred.
1–3 years of experience in emergency management, catastrophe planning, disaster response, data analysis, business continuity, logistics, or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and communicate data to support operational planning and business decision-making.
Experience using mapping, GIS, data visualization, or reporting tools to analyze and communicate geographic and operational information.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, evaluate potential impacts, and translate data into actionable information.
Knowledge of emergency management, disaster preparedness, response, and recovery principles.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate complex information clearly to a variety of audiences.
Proven interpersonal and collaboration skills for working effectively across business units and with internal and external partners.
Ability to remain flexible and effectively support operations during catastrophe events and other time-sensitive situations.
Relevant training or certifications in emergency management, GIS, data analytics, business continuity, or disaster recovery are preferred.
Experience in the insurance industry, including property, auto, and claims operations is a plus but not required.

Travel Requirements

Occasional travel to support CAT readiness exercises, business meetings, training, field operations, or catastrophe response activities.

Additionally, for full time positions, you will be eligible to participate in our incentive program based upon the achievement of organization, team and personal performance.

Enemix is partnering with a leading OEM here in Australia on a key leadership hire for their Brisbane operation. This is a chance to step into a role where you won’t just run projects, you’ll set how projects are run across the entire business.

The Role

Within this Senior Project Manager role you’ll lead a team of Project Managers as well as a Project Coordinator, owning delivery of the project portfolio from contract award and kick-off through to commissioning, handover, and defects liability. You’ll work closely with engineers, electricians, field technicians, and the wider business to deliver work on customer sites across Australia, including regional and remote locations.

What you’ll be doing

Leading, mentoring and developing a team of Project Managers, building depth so delivery never hinges on one person
Setting practical project governance standards (stage gates, approvals, templates) that control risk without drowning the team in admin
Owning project budgets, forecasts and margins alongside Finance, including monthly cost-to-complete reviews
Aligning schedules to customer construction programs, equipment lead times and grid-connection milestones
Allocating the shared field workforce across concurrent projects, balancing utilisation with fatigue management and leave
Acting as the senior point of contact for customers and executive stakeholders
Working with head office in Spain to keep equipment and materials moving on time
Leading visible safety leadership on site and driving lessons learned and continuous improvement

What you’ll bring

5+ years in project management, with at least 3 years leading project teams
A strong grasp of electrical systems, inverters, drives and battery technology
Experience delivering multiple complex projects at once, ideally in solar, BESS, or high-voltage electrical environments
Solid commercial and budget management capability
Knowledge of safety management systems, Codes of Practice and relevant standards
A degree in Engineering, Business or a related field, or a Cert IV in Project Management
PMP, PRINCE2 or Agile certification is highly regarded
Confidence with tools such as MS Project, Smartsheet, Excel and ideally SAP

What’s on offer

A senior leadership role with genuine influence over how the business delivers
Backing from a global OEM with a strong pipeline in the Australian market
Brisbane-based (Eagle Farm), with travel to project sites

Inverters and battery energy storage systems are at the heart of how Australia’s grid is changing. The person in this seat will directly shape how that equipment gets delivered, commissioned and handed over on projects that are moving the energy transition forward across the nation.
